text: dsh-quberi 是把 Quberi 知识库接入 DeepSeek Harness 的插件，通过 /quberi 命令完成 OAuth 登录，并注册搜索、图片查找、浏览空间与文档、阅读段落上下文、保存笔记和上传文件等工具。搜索可按文本、图片或两者查找，并可限定空间；浏览工具列出可访问内容及文档状态。适合希望在 Harness 对话中查阅团队资料、保存讨论结论或加入工作区文件的用户。需要 Quberi 账号和 Quberi 服务；文件上传默认提供，须为每个文件单独确认。

dsh-quberi connects Quberi to DeepSeek Harness. Sign in with /quberi, then search documents or pictures, browse spaces and files, read around passages, and save notes. Searches target a space and use text, pictures, or both. Upload workspace files with per-file approval. Requires a Quberi account.
dsh-quberi 的功能「知识搜索」：用问题或关键词搜索可读空间中的文档段落，可指定空间和返回数量，并可设置只搜文本或同时查找相关图片。
dsh-quberi 的功能「图片查找」：输入外观描述即可搜索可访问空间内已索引的图片，可限定空间并查看匹配预览。
dsh-quberi 的功能「浏览知识库」：列出可读空间及可编辑状态，也能按空间分页查看文档名称、类型、大小、更新时间和索引状态。
dsh-quberi 的功能「保存笔记」：提供标题、Markdown 正文和可选空间，将对话结论或计划保存为知识库文档，默认写入个人空间。
dsh-quberi 的功能「上传工作区文件」：选择工作区中的单个受支持文件并指定目的空间；Harness 会显示文件信息并逐次请求确认后再上传。
dsh-quberi 使用前须知：登录及知识库操作连接 Quberi API 与 OAuth 服务；搜索、保存和上传会向所配置的 Quberi 服务发送数据。默认地址为 api.quberi.com 和 ai.quberi.com。

dsh-quberi README · dsh-quberi：Query your [Quberi](https://ai.quberi.com) knowledge base from DeepSeek Harness:
search, browse, save notes and upload files.

The interesting part isn't the search — it's what search is allowed to return.
Quberi enforces permissions **per document**, not per space: two people asking
the same question in the same space can get different answers, because the
retrieval filter runs inside the vector index and a denied document is never a
candidate in the first place.

dsh-quberi README · dsh-quberi：- Per-document access rules with **deny wins** — a grant cannot override a
  decision to hide one document.
- **Filtered at retrieval time**, so you get a full result set, not a shorter
  one with holes.
- **Revoked picture links die** — a picture preview URL issued before access was
  removed returns 404 on the next request.
- Writes go only into spaces you can edit; uploads require your confirmation
  each time.

dsh-quberi README · dsh-quberi：Ask Harness a question about your documents. The first time, your browser
opens by itself so you can approve access; after that the model can call
`quberi_search`, which finds passages in the documents **you** can read in
Quberi, in the one organization you pick (name a space to search only that one). It can also call `quberi_save` to add
a note (a conclusion, decision or summary from the chat) to your knowledge base,
and `quberi_upload_file` to add a file from your workspace. `quberi_list_spaces`
and `quberi_list_documents` show what is there, and `quberi_search_images` finds
pictures from a description and shows them in the chat. Saving is new in 0.3.0
and uploading in 0.4.0; each needs a fresh sign-in that includes it. Browsing and
picture search need nothing beyond search. An
upload only happens after **you approve that file** (see Uploading files).

dsh-quberi README · dsh-quberi：Each scope is granted on its own: search needs `knowledge:read`, saving needs
`knowledge:write` and uploading needs `knowledge:upload`. A document someone
shared with you individually is found even if you cannot read its space, and a
document hidden from you is not found even if you can read its space.

dsh-quberi README · Install：In DeepSeek Harness open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter:

```
dsh-quberi
```

Or from a terminal (replace `desktop` with your profile name):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-quberi
```

Then restart Harness. To upgrade, remove the old version first
(`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-quberi`), then add it again.

You need a Quberi account at [ai.quberi.com](https://ai.quberi.com), or your own
Quberi server (see Configuration).

dsh-quberi README · Install：A plugin runs on your machine with your permissions, so read the source first.
It is small: `src/oauth.ts` (sign-in helpers), `src/browser.ts` (opens your
browser), `src/controller.ts` (sign-in, token refresh, search, save, upload),
`src/upload.ts` (which files may be uploaded, and the approval gate) and
`src/index.ts` (the `/quberi` command and the tools). Its only runtime
dependency is `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`.

dsh-quberi README · From source：```sh
npm install
npm test
npm pack      # builds lib/ and writes dsh-quberi-<version>.tgz
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /path/to/dsh-quberi-<version>.tgz

dsh-quberi README · Use：| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/quberi login` | Opens your browser to sign in to Quberi (the link is also shown in case it does not open). Choose an organization and allow. You rarely need this: the first search does it for you. If you signed in with an older version, run it again to allow saving or uploading. |
| `/quberi status` | Shows whether you are connected. Never prints a token. |
| `/quberi logout` | Revokes the sign-in at Quberi and forgets it locally. |
| `/quberi mode [text\|image\|both]` | Shows or sets where searches look: the documents' text, pictures, or both (the default). See Where a search looks. |

dsh-quberi README · Use：The sign-in page says what Harness is asking to do (search, save notes, upload files) and
what it cannot do, and lets you choose the organization (shown here in Chinese):

You can also disconnect any time in Quberi under **Account → Connected tools**.

When sign-in finishes, the browser shows a confirmation page and Harness is
brought back to the front (macOS). Nothing needs to be copied or pasted.

dsh-quberi README · Use：On a machine with no screen (a remote shell), the browser is not opened; the
plugin gives you the link to open on another device instead.

dsh-quberi README · Before it works：The organization you choose must allow outside tools. It is **off by default**.
An owner or admin turns it on under **Admin console → Integrations → Outside
tools**; owners and admins also get a "Turn on" button on the approval page.

dsh-quberi README · What leaves Quberi：The passages the search returns go to Harness and to whichever AI model Harness
uses. Quberi's "check before sending" step does not apply to this path. Every
search is recorded in the organization's audit log (the tool's name and the
documents returned, never the question or the text).

dsh-quberi README · What leaves Quberi：`quberi_read_around` sends more of a document than the search does: up to 3000 characters on
either side of a passage, only when the model asks for it, and only from documents you can open
in Quberi. Each call is recorded in the audit log (the document, the version and how many
characters, never the text) and is rate limited. A page image is fetched by Harness from a
short-lived link on your Quberi address; the link names one page for you and stops working when
you sign out of the tool, lose access to the document or after about ten minutes. An organization
owner can turn outside tools off, which ends all of this at once.

dsh-quberi README · Saving notes：`quberi_save` takes a title, the note text (Markdown) and, optionally, the name
of a space. With no space it saves into **your personal space**. The tool asks
the model to offer to save and wait for you to agree, not to save silently, but
that is an instruction to the model, not a guarantee: you decide by what you
approve and by watching what the model does.

dsh-quberi README · Saving notes：Here the person asked Harness to save the conversation to their personal space. The model
calls `quberi_save`, then says where the note went and when it becomes searchable:

A saved note becomes a document in that space. **Anyone who can read that space
can find it**, so name a shared space only on purpose. Saving is recorded in
the audit log (the tool's name and the new document, not the text).

dsh-quberi README · Where in the file a passage is：When your Quberi server records it, each passage comes with its place, so the answer can say where to look in the
original: the page of a PDF (`page 3`, `pages 3-4`), the slide of a presentation, the sheet and row of a spreadsheet,
the heading and paragraph of a Word file, or the lines of a text file. The version is shown when the file has more
than one (`version 1 (older, replaced by version 2)`). A passage read from a scan, or a model's description of a
picture, is marked as such, because it can contain mistakes. Nothing is shown for a passage the server gave no place
for, and an older server leaves the results exactly as before.
section: Where in the file a passage is

text:
dsh-quberi README · Citing a passage：When your Quberi server sends it, each passage comes with a `Cite as:` line (for example
`handbook.pdf, page 3, version 2 (latest)`), and the model is asked to end each point it takes from a passage
with that line, copied as given, and never to state a page or version the line does not give. This is a request
to the model, not something Harness can enforce. A passage with no recorded place is cited by its document alone.
dsh-quberi README · Seeing the page, and reading around a passage：Two more things come with a search result, when your Quberi server supports them.
section: Seeing the page, and reading around a passage

text:
dsh-quberi README · Seeing the page, and reading around a passage：**The page.** A passage from a PDF (and text read out of a picture) comes with a link to an image of the
page it was found on. The result gives the model a ready-made `` line and tells it to show the
page only when you ask to see the original. Slides, spreadsheets and Word files have no page that can be
drawn, so they carry no image; their place (slide, sheet and row, paragraph) is still named. Harness only
passes on a link that is on your Quberi address and in the page path; any other link is dropped.
section: Seeing the page, and reading around a passage

text:
dsh-quberi README · Seeing the page, and reading around a passage：**The text around it.** `quberi_read_around` returns the text before and after a passage, from the same
file and version, so the model can read it in context without you opening the file. The search result
gives the model the exact values to pass (`document_id`, `version`, `char_start`, `char_end`), and the
model is told to ask only when you want more context or a passage looks cut off. It does not work for
text read from a scan or a picture, which has no text layer to read around, and it says so.
section: Seeing the page, and reading around a passage

text:
dsh-quberi README · Where a search looks：A text search cannot see pictures, so by default `quberi_search` looks in both: it
returns the matching passages and, beside them, a few pictures that **might** be what
you asked for (for example, asking about "动物母狮" shows the lioness picture even though
no document mentions it). The pictures are offered as possible matches, never as the answer,
and only ones scoring above a floor are included. Without this, asking for a picture by
its subject would have said "nothing found".

dsh-quberi README · Where a search looks：In this example the question is "VMC-850 的设备铭牌和开机前检查" (the nameplate of a machine and
its pre-start checks). The model searches, then answers from the operating procedure and
shows the nameplate picture it found next to the text. The text documents say nothing about
the nameplate itself; the picture does.

dsh-quberi README · Where a search looks：- Say "only the documents" or "only pictures" and the model sets `kind` to `text` or `image`.
- `/quberi mode text` or `/quberi mode image` fixes it for you, and overrides the model;
  `/quberi mode both` goes back to the default. In `text` mode the picture tool refuses.
  The choice lasts until Harness restarts; set the default with `searchMode` (below).

dsh-quberi README · Where a search looks：- `both` needs a Quberi server that supports it. An older server only searches text, and
  the plugin simply gets no pictures.
- Looking for pictures runs Quberi's picture model, so it has its own rate limit. If that
  is reached, or picture search is off, the text results still come back.

dsh-quberi README · Finding pictures：`quberi_search_images` finds pictures from a description ("a red bracket with two
holes") in the documents you can read, closest first, optionally in one named space.
Harness cannot show a picture a tool returns, but it does show a Markdown image
in the model's reply, so each result carries a link to a small preview (a JPEG of
at most 320 px) and the model is asked to paste it into its answer exactly as
given. Three things follow from that:
- The link is short-lived (about ten minutes) and names one picture for you. It
  works without a sign-in header, so anyone who has the link can open that one
  small preview until it expires. It stops working at once if you revoke this
  tool in Quberi, lose access to the space, or the picture is deleted or archived.
- The model has to copy the link without changing it. That is a request, not a
  guarantee: a model can drop or alter it, and then no preview appears. Ask again.
- The plugin only passes on links that point at your Quberi address, so a reply
  cannot send the chat window to some other site.
The search runs the same space isolation as text search, and each use is recorded
in the audit log (the pi

dsh-quberi README · Browsing：`quberi_list_spaces` lists the spaces you can read: your personal space and the
team spaces, how many documents each holds, and whether you can edit it (so
whether saving or uploading there would work). `quberi_list_documents` lists the
documents in one space you name, newest first: name, type, size, last update and
whether it is searchable yet. It returns up to 50 at a time and hands the model a
cursor for the next page. Pass `type` (`image`, `pdf`, `word`, `spreadsheet`,
`presentation`, `text` or `other`) to list only that kind of file; this needs a
Quberi server that supports it (an older one ignores the filter).

dsh-quberi README · Browsing：Asked "which spaces and documents do I have?", the model lists the spaces first and then
each space's documents. Pictures are marked as searchable by picture, text files by content.

dsh-quberi README · Browsing：Both listing tools show file information only. They never return what is inside a document
(that is what search is for) and they do not say who uploaded it. They use the
same read permission as search and the same live access rules, so a space or
document you cannot see in Quberi is not listed. Each use is recorded in the
audit log (which kind of listing and how many items, never the names).

dsh-quberi README · How it shows up in Harness：Harness lists a plugin's tool calls as plain rows ("Tool call · quberi_search"
plus a summary of the arguments) and does not display custom cards from
plugins. What you read is the model's own answer. The tools therefore return
plain text, and ask the model to answer in your language, to show spaces as a
list and documents as a table, to name the document each point comes from, and
not to wrap any of it in a code block. That is a request to the model, not a
guarantee, so the layout can vary between models. The upload approval prompt is
different: Harness itself shows it, with the file, its size and the destination.
section: How it shows up in Harness

text:
dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：`quberi_upload_file` sends one file from your current workspace to your personal
space, or to a named space you can edit. It exists so Harness can keep a PDF,
a Word or Excel file, a slide deck, an image or a text file you point to,
without you opening the Quberi web app.

Harness asks before each file leaves the workspace, showing the file, its size and the
destination:

dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：Afterwards the model lists what is in the space. Files that are still being indexed are
marked as not yet searchable; the saved note is already searchable:

Because a model chooses the path, and a model can be steered by whatever text it
read last, three separate checks stand between a path and the network:

dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：1. **You approve every file.** Harness shows the exact file, its size, a short
   hash and the destination space, and the upload runs only if you allow it. The
   approval covers that one file once; there is no "always allow". With no
   approval prompt available (a headless run), or in the "full access, never ask"
   mode, the upload is refused rather than sent.
2. **Workspace only.** The path must stay inside the workspace folder after links
   are resolved. Folders such as `.git`, `.ssh` and `.aws`, and names that look
   like secrets (`.env*`, `secrets.json`, `credentials.txt`, `id_rsa*`), are
   refused outright. This filter is best effort, not a guarantee, which is why
   step 1 exists.
3. **The approved file is the file sent.** The file is read again when it is
   sent and must match what you approved; if it changed, nothing is uploaded.

dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：Quberi then checks the file's actual content (not its name or label) and has the
final word: png, jpeg, gif, webp, pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, md, csv, txt and json
are accepted, up to 25 MB. Archives, HTML, SVG, executables and legacy `.doc` /
`.xls` are refused. PDF, Office, Markdown, CSV, text and JSON files are indexed
for search after upload, which is not instant: about a minute for a short note,
several minutes for a large PDF. Until a file is indexed, search cannot find it;
a search tells the model which documents are still being indexed so it can say so
instead of presenting unrelated passages as the answer. A picture is indexed by
what it shows, so `quberi_search_images` can find it from a description (when
your Quberi server has picture search); `quberi_search` itself returns text
passages only.

dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：A space owner can ask that uploads be approved first. In such a space, a file uploaded by
someone who is not an owner or admin of the space waits as pending: it is not indexed, so
search cannot find it or quote it, and only the uploader and the space's reviewers can see
it. The upload tool reports it as waiting for approval instead of as done. An owner or admin
then approves it, which queues it for indexing, or rejects it with a reason. Owners and
admins upload straight in. Here four files are uploaded to a space that asks for approval:

dsh-quberi README · Uploading files：After the reviewer has decided, asking the model for the files' state shows the outcome: two
approved and searchable, two rejected.

Anyone who can read the destination space can find the file. Uploading is a
separate permission (`knowledge:upload`), recorded in the audit log as the
document and its size and type, never the contents. To turn the tool off, and
stop asking for the permission at sign-in, set `uploadFiles: false` (see
Configuration).

dsh-quberi README · What it can and cannot do：- It acts as you: search only reads spaces you can read, and save only writes
  into spaces you can edit. Both are re-checked on every call. If your access
  changes, the next call reflects it.
- It can add notes and files, nothing else. It cannot edit or delete anything
  that is already there.
- Saving (`knowledge:write`) and uploading (`knowledge:upload`) are separate
  permissions. A sign-in made by an earlier version does not have them and is
  not upgraded behind your back; run `/quberi login` to add them.
- Access tokens last one hour and refresh on their own; a sign-in lasts at most
  90 days. A refresh token that is used twice is treated as stolen and the whole
  sign-in is revoked.
- Turning outside tools off for the organization, or disconnecting in Quberi,
  stops the very next search or save.
section: What it can and cannot do

text:
dsh-quberi README · Configuration：Defaults are right for the hosted service. For a self-hosted Quberi, point
`baseUrl` at your API (https, or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` for development).
Signing in happens on the server that publishes `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
and names itself as `issuer`. On the hosted service that is `https://ai.quberi.com`; for a
self-hosted Quberi it is the same origin as `baseUrl`, so you normally set nothing. Only if
your sign-in server is on a different origin than your API, set `authUrl` to it.
`openBrowser`, `autoLogin` and `focusApp` (all on by default) switch off the
automatic browser, sign-in on first use, and returning to Harness. `uploadFiles`
(on by default) offers the upload tool; off removes it. `searchMode` (`both` by default,
or `text` or `image`) is where searches look until you change it with `/quberi mode`:

dsh-quberi README · Compatibility：Built and tested against `@deepseek-ai/*` `0.2.0-rc.2`. Harness is a developer
preview and its plugin interfaces can change. The token set is stored with the
credential-record API (`credentials.modifyRecord`) so two Harness processes
cannot overwrite each other's rotated refresh token.
